## Summary

All changes are in `crates/polars-plan/src/plans/aexpr/predicates/skip_batches.rs` (the core logic behind `Expr._skip_batch_predicate`). The Python bindings just forward to this function, so no change was needed there.

Previously, `does_dtype_have_sufficient_order` returned `false` for all floats, so float columns never produced a skip-batch predicate anywhere. I kept that function as the gate for non-float ordered types and added NaN-aware handling for floats in each relevant branch.

**New helpers:**
- `lv_is_definitely_not_nan` — true only when a literal is a *known* concrete non-NaN value (unknown/non-literal constants are treated conservatively).
- `lv_is_definitely_nan` — true only when a literal is a *known* NaN.
- `float_inequality_is_skippable` — normalizes the operator so the column is on the left (swapping `Lt↔Gt`, `LtEq↔GtEq` when the literal is on the left), then allows `<`/`<=` for any literal and `>`/`>=` only when the literal is NaN.

**Per-branch behavior for float columns (matching the spec):**
- **`Lt` / `LtEq`** → predicate generated for any literal (incl. NaN); NaN never satisfies `<`/`<=`, so hidden NaN can't be wrongly skipped.
- **`Gt` / `GtEq`** → predicate only when the literal is NaN (nothing is `>`/`>=` NaN); non-NaN literals return `None` because a hidden NaN (largest under Polars ordering) would satisfy them but is invisible to NaN-excluding statistics.
- **`Eq` / `EqValidity`** → predicate only when the literal is a known non-NaN value; NaN literal returns `None`.
- **`NotEq` / `NotEqValidity`** → still `None` for floats (unchanged — falls through the order gate), since hidden NaN always satisfies inequality.
- **Reversed operands** (literal on the left) → handled by the operator-swap in `float_inequality_is_skippable`, so e.g. `lit(5.0) > col(x)` is treated as `col(x) < 5.0` → non-`None`.
- **`is_between`** → predicate only when both bounds are known non-NaN constants; `None` if either bound is NaN.
- **`is_in`** left unchanged (still `None` for floats — conservative and safe).

The generated predicates rely on `is_stat_defined`, which already guards float min/max stats with an `is_not_nan` check, so all-NaN batches degrade safely to "don't skip."

The note about existing parquet-scan tests switching `>` to `<` on float columns is a test-side change, which per your instructions is applied automatically by the verification harness — I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
